national_raw_news.title: Asian Para Games begin in Japan; Over 150 athletes from India to aim for over 100 medals
national_raw_news.content: The Asian Para Games 2026 began today in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with India aiming to build on its record medal haul at the previous edition. The fifth edition of the continental sporting event will run until October 24, featuring competitions across 18 sports. The opening ceremony was held at Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Nagoya under the theme, “WABI: We Are Beautiful Individuals”. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi welcomed athletes and officials from across Asia. India is targeting a 100-medal haul, with para-athletics head coach Satyanarayana expressing confidence in the contingent’s preparation, determination and ability to deliver a strong performance. At the 2023 edition in Hangzhou, China, India achieved a historic milestone by winning a record 111 medals. Para-badminton player Pramod Bhagat and sprinter Simran Sharma are leading the Indian contingent as flag-bearers. India has sent a 281-member contingent, including 168 athletes and 113 officials and support staff. The athletes, comprising 112 men and 56 women, will compete in 11 disciplines. The Indian squad includes prominent para-athletes such as javelin thrower Sumit Antil, shooter Avani Lekhara, archer Sheetal Devi, sprinter Simran Sharma, Pramod Bhagat and Bhavina Patel. The event will be streamed live on the Waves OTT app and Prasar Bharati Sports’ YouTube channel.

national_raw_news.content: Durga Puja is being celebrated with religious fervour and traditional enthusiasm across Odisha today, with beautifully decorated pandals and temples drawing large numbers of devotees. Special rituals are being performed at Shakti Peethas, while major cities, including Bhubaneswar and Cuttack, are witnessing festive gatherings and elaborate decorations. The celebrations reflect Odisha’s rich cultural heritage and the enduring significance of Goddess Durga as the symbol of divine power and the triumph of good over evil. Tripura is immersed in the festive spirit of Durga Puja, with celebrations underway across the state. Devotees and visitors are thronging puja pandals to offer prayers and seek the blessings of Goddess Durga. Colourful illuminations, beautifully decorated pandals and festive activities have created a vibrant atmosphere in various localities. In a resounding testament to cultural heritage and communal unity, the Bengali-speaking Barak Valley of Assam has immersed itself in the grand celebrations of Durga Puja. Beyond its religious significance, Durga Puja in Barak Valley stands out as a unique symbol of interfaith harmony. In a beautiful confluence of cultures, members of both the Hindu and Muslim communities actively join hands during the festivities. From Muslim artisans contributing to the intricate pandal artwork and light setups to local volunteers helping manage crowds and welcoming visitors, the festival transcends religious boundaries to become a shared socio-cultural extravaganza for the entire valley.

national_raw_news.title: Kenya’s Charles Matata breaks course record to win men’s elite race at Vedanta Delhi Half Marathon 11 hours ago 182
national_raw_news.content: Kenya’s Charles Matata broke the course record to win the men’s elite race at the Vedanta Delhi Half Marathon today, while Ethiopia’s Wudinesh Alemu claimed the women’s title. Matata clocked 58 minutes, 52 seconds over the 21.097-kilometre course, shaving one second off the previous record set by Ethiopia’s Amedework Walelegn in 2020. Matata set the record to earn an additional 12,000 dollars on top of the 27,000 dollar winner’s prize. Kenya swept the men’s podium, with Samwel Nyamai Mailu finishing second in 59 minutes, 24 seconds and Stanley Waithaka Mburu third in 59 minutes, 33 seconds. Alemu won the women’s race in 1 hour, 6 minutes, 35 seconds. Kenya’s Selah Businei finished second in 1 hour, 7 minutes, 1 second, followed by Cynthia Chelangat Chepkwony in 1 hour, 7 minutes, 32 seconds. In the Indian elite men’s race, Shailesh Kushwaha won in one hour, five minutes and five seconds, ahead of Gaurav Mathur in one hour, five minutes and 11 seconds, and Hemant Kumar in one hour, five minutes and 37 seconds. Ankita Dhyani won the Indian elite women’s title in one hour, 12 minutes and 46 seconds. Soniya finished second in one hour, 14 minutes and 56 seconds, while Bhagirathi was third in one hour, 15 minutes and 51 seconds. Union Minister Kiren Rijiju, Chief of Defence Staff Gen. N.S. Raja Subramani and World Athletics Vice President Adille Sumariwalla attended the event. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta flagged off the Great Delhi Run.
